clue.text: Modelling a solo performance, according to the Just So Stories

definitions.meaning: the fashion world's raised runway stands for the whole business of showing clothes

definitions.text: a solo performance, according to the Just So Stories
definitions.meaning: Kipling's tale 'The Cat That Walked by Himself' is a lone stroll by a cat

explanation.surface: Someone describes modelling as a one-person act, citing Kipling's children's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The Just So Stories are Rudyard Kipling's children's tales; one is 'The Cat That Walked by Himself', a walk taken solo by a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway for fashion shows is the familiar shorthand for the profession of modelling clothes.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot picture with high tension — it's illegal

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise its hammer ready for firing
fig. is short for figure, an illustration in a book
HT is the standard electrical abbreviation for high tension

explanation.surface: Readying a gun for a tense photo shoot turns out to be against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare to shoot' suggests photography beside 'picture', but it is about a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting birds to battle each other for sport is banned in Britain, so this bloodsport is unlawful.

clue.text: What Omar glimpsed within the tavern — is it Very?

definitions.text: What Omar glimpsed within the tavern — is it Very?

parts.words: What Omar glimpsed within the tavern — is it Very?
parts.note: FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam prefers one glimpse of divine radiance caught in the tavern to it lost in the temple; a Very light is a signal flare, and very once meant true

explanation.surface: A question about what the Persian poet saw in a drinking house, and whether it was a flare.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured flare fired from a pistol; 'very' also has the old sense 'true', as in 'very God of very God'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubaiyat stanza names the divine illumination Omar would rather glimpse in the inn than miss in the temple.

clue.text: Country of 7, say

annotationWithheld.why: Country of 7, say (6): the wordplay is the answer to 7-down read as instructions (LO from 'look' turned back, inside ANGA, 'anger' said aloud), so the indicators 'back' and 'in' are not clue words; the grammar cannot express it

clue.text: Girl entertaining artist with chop?

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them within, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Kate is a girl's name
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A young woman plays host to a painter who has a smart haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop' looks like a haircut or a cut of meat; the karate chop is the martial-arts blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese martial art is famed for the edge-of-hand strike called a chop.

clue.text: Choice was first preserved

parts.note: your pick is your choice
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: The selected item came out on top in being preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: Food kept in vinegar or brine has been preserved this way.

clue.text: Father — he's left off being forceful — flags

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: something left off is omitted, so these two letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: vehement means forceful and intense
the pronoun gives the letters to drop; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: Dad has stopped being so assertive, and his energy is fading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like a verb meaning tires; it is a noun, the flat paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstones are the slabs laid to make a footway, so a footpath is made of them.

clue.text: A number of mysterious utterances on boats

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
oracles are cryptic prophetic pronouncements

explanation.surface: Several riddling prophecies are delivered aboard some vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link here; coracles are small round wickerwork boats used in Wales and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Coracles are small round wicker-and-hide river craft, a kind of boat.

clue.text: Play in retrospect fashionable — the rage?

parts.note: to look back is to view things in retrospect
in means fashionable
rage means anger

explanation.surface: A drama, seen in hindsight, is trendy and all the rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The rage' suggests a craze, following 'fashionable', but it is simply fury. John Osborne's 1956 play is the drama.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne's 1956 drama is the play that launched the Angry Young Men.

clue.text: School at first in academic outburst

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of another, splitting it

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
Eton is the famous English public school
I is the Roman numeral one, the first

explanation.surface: A school breaks out at the start of a scholarly row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like a beginning-letter signal, but AT is taken as written and 'first' gives I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: An explosion is a violent bursting out, so it fits outburst.

clue.text: Horsefly (colloquially horse) as deputy

parts.note: a cleg is a dialect name for a horsefly
a gee or gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, and G stands for gee

explanation.surface: An insect pest, informally called a horse, serves as a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg was Britain's Deputy Prime Minister from 2010 to 2015, when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Clegg served as Deputy Prime Minister in the coalition government, the topical deputy of the day.

clue.text: Take one sort of word — "grass" — for craft with shallow draft

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take
I is the Roman numeral one
a verb is one kind of word, a part of speech
oats are a cereal grass

explanation.surface: Instructions to pick a word meaning grass, to describe a vessel that sits high in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the slang verb for inform, sitting by 'word', but it is the plant OAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddle steamers on rivers like the Mississippi were built with shallow draft for shallow water.

clue.text: Pawnbroker and taxman keeping Cams' problem from Stowe

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: the economist James Tobin proposed the Tobin tax on currency trades

indicators.note: a problem here is a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker and a tax official are saddled with the trouble of a Cambridge river.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker; the Tobin tax was proposed by the economist James Tobin. Harriet Beecher Stowe wrote the 1852 anti-slavery novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe's best-known novel is the abolitionist classic of 1852.

clue.text: Whence reward for wisdom? Faith? Love? Try love

definitions.text: Whence reward for wisdom? Faith? Love? Try love

indicators.note: the whole question asks for a source, telling the solver to work the following words into the answer

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
love again gives O

explanation.surface: Musing on where a prize for being wise comes from: faith, or love, or just trying again.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words FAITH, O, TRY, O are rearranged. A wisdom tooth is a molar, so the coin-leaving fairy who pays for lost teeth is the 'reward for wisdom'.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk figure who leaves money under a pillow for a shed tooth is where such a reward comes from.

clue.text: The curse of the 10 15

indicators.note: the word sits inside the run formed by the two answers it belongs to

parts.note: these numbers stand for the answers to 10-across and 15-down

explanation.surface: A mysterious curse attached to two numbered things.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers stand for RIVERBOAT and HELSINKI; read together, they hold the four letters across the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word or profanity is a curse, an old sense of a solemn promise word.

clue.text: Charge less than German joiner and truce breaker

parts.note: und is German for and, a joining word

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German carpenter and a ceasefire violator undersell the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' looks like a carpenter; it is the conjunction 'and'. 'Breaker' rearranges TRUCE into ERCUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell more cheaply than a rival is to price below them.

clue.text: Most of the sun's about to set on the Baltic

indicators.note: one piece goes around another
only the greater part of the word is kept, its end removed

parts.note: Helios is the Greek sun god, the sun personified
the sun sinks as it sets

explanation.surface: Much of the sun is about to go down over the northern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Finland's capital is a port city on the Gulf of Finland, an arm of the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Walker gets right inside the wire

annotationWithheld.why: Walker gets right inside the wire (8): TEAM comes from 'side' and the container sign from 'in', both inside the single word 'inside', which therefore does two jobs and cannot be split into leaves
annotationWithheld.clue: Walker gets right inside the wire

clue.text: Stressed when Greek cross put on Turkish island Ordnance Survey missed out

indicators.note: one piece is placed in front of the other in the answer

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T, the shape of a T-cross

indicators.note: something missed out is omitted, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Tenedos is the old name of Bozcaada, an island off Turkey
OS is the abbreviation for Ordnance Survey, Britain's mapping agency

explanation.surface: A Greek cross is placed on an Aegean island the mapmakers forgot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is the UK's national mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tautened has been pulled tight, put under tension or stress.

clue.text: Dog, noisy one, one with no tail

parts.note: f is forte, loud in music
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: this one stands for a dog, the creature just named

explanation.surface: A dog: a loud one, and one missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Fido is the stock name for a pet dog. Solvers tempted by DIN for 'noisy' get DINO, which isn't a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Fido is the traditional generic pet name for a dog.

clue.text: Seemed pleased with conveyance including motorway

indicators.note: a thing including another contains it

parts.note: a sled is a sledge, a means of conveyance
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: Someone looked happy riding a vehicle that took in a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: To smile is to look pleased, so the past tense matches seemed pleased.

clue.text: Evasive throw about 12 inches

indicators.note: one piece goes round another

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
twelve inches are one foot, written I (one) FT

explanation.surface: A slippery character hurls something about a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About 12 inches' looks like an approximate length; 'about' is the container sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A shifty person is untrustworthy and evasive in manner.

clue.text: Adult female has order to get on with it

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A grown woman is told to stop dawdling and get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads as a command but rearranges ADULT FEMALE HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The command to proceed at maximum speed urges someone to press on with a task.

clue.text: Quantities coming up — hold it!

indicators.note: in a down light, coming up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: pots of money means large quantities

explanation.surface: Large amounts are arriving, so wait!
explanation.definitionFit: The command to halt and the exclamation 'hold it!' are interchangeable.

clue.text: Mostly a lot of skill in contriving real trouble

indicators.note: a lot of a word is its greater part, here its first five letters

parts.note: ingenuity is cleverness in devising things

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Much talent in devising things leads to real difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' rearranges REAL into ERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning usually or on the whole, as mostly does.

clue.text: See 1 down
Rare earth that long ago briefly gained a lot of success

parts.note: yt was the old written abbreviation for 'that', y standing for the thorn letter

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its end trimmed

parts.note: a triumph is a great success

explanation.surface: Something achieved in the past brought great success.
explanation.walkthrough: In old writing 'yt' abbreviated 'that', the y being the obsolete letter thorn. 'Gained' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttrium is usually grouped with the rare-earth metals in chemistry.

clue.text: Party I'd arranged for excursion

indicators.note: arranged letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has organised a do as an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A day trip is an outing there and back on the same day, an excursion.
